name: VA-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+6 district with a Democratic incumbent running for re-election
Roughly 15-to-1 fundraising advantage for Subramanyam ($1.6M raised vs. $107K)
Both major prediction markets price Democrats near 97%
No public polling or expert ratings, keeping uncertainty elevated
model.rationale: The district's six-point Democratic lean, Subramanyam's dominant fundraising edge, and prediction markets pricing Democratic victory at about 97 percent all point the same way. With no public polling, the expected margin sits near nineteen points with wide uncertainty, but the win probability remains well above the Safe threshold.
model.watch: Fresh polling showing a single-digit race, significant outside spending for Beckwith, or a sharp national shift toward Republicans could move this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Virginia's 10th District leans Democratic by about six points, and incumbent Suhas Subramanyam is seeking re-election with the usual advantages of incumbency. He has raised roughly 1.6 million dollars, more than ten times what Republican Dave Beckwith has reported, and holds a large cash-on-hand edge. Outside spending on either side has been negligible so far. Independent Ahsen Malik is also on the ballot but shows no visible fundraising.

Neither side has released public general-election polling, and no expert raters currently list the race. Prediction markets on both major platforms price a Democratic win at about 97 percent, in line with the district's lean and the financial gap. The forecast therefore rates Virginia's 10th as Safe Democratic, with an expected margin near nineteen points and moderate uncertainty given the absence of polls.
